description: Edits or reads a chart already open in the chat (from chart_open): switch market or timeframe, add or remove a native indicator, draw a level or a zone, clear drawings, or zoom to a date range; {op: "read"} changes nothing and returns what the chart shows now. Ops apply in order. Usually waits a few seconds for the chart to confirm and returns what it shows, in words, with the numbers the user sees on it: the last price, the change since the day's open (00:00 UTC), the high and low of the visible range and each indicator's latest value (e.g. "RSI 38.2"). Quote those as of the moment of the reply; it never returns candles. {op: "read", image: true} also sends a picture of the chart as the user sees it into your context, where the chat app accepts images from the chart (it arrives with the next message). If the chart is idle it may answer at once that the edits are queued and when the chart applies them; if it is not on screen, edits stay queued and apply when it is shown again, and a read returns its last report without live numbers. Use chart_open instead to show a new chart.

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

image.description: Also send a picture of the chart as the user sees it into your context (only where the chat app accepts images from the chart).

name: chart_command
title: Vela chart change
